headline: High: gpt-engineer can write and execute code in a shared project directory, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways with dbt-core.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can read warehouse-derived project artifacts and gpt-engineer writes files in the shared project directory, so attacker-controlled content can cross from one agent into the other through files. This is not a direct instruction channel, but the shared workspace makes prompt injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer reads dbt-generated files as instructions or prompts
IF both agents operate in the same project directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as prompts
Add a manual review step before gpt-engineer consumes dbt outputs
Use provenance labels on files exchanged between agents
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or read-only mounts

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while gpt-engineer reads and writes the project directory and can call external models. Shared files can therefore move sensitive warehouse-derived content into gpt-engineer's context and onward to a third-party API.
conditions: IF warehouse-derived data is written into the shared project directory
IF gpt-engineer sends that file content to its configured model backend
mitigations: Keep sensitive warehouse outputs out of the shared project directory
Redact secrets and identifiers before handoff
Restrict gpt-engineer to synthetic or sampled data
Review outbound prompts for sensitive fields before execution
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on file ingestion

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has write_filesystem and per-project shared state, while dbt-core calls a data warehouse and may also operate on project files. Their overlapping access to the same project directory creates write contention and inconsistent artifacts, though dbt-core lacks filesystem write capability in the profile so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same project files in one session
IF dbt-core-generated artifacts are consumed before gpt-engineer finishes writing
mitigations: Serialize access to the project directory
Use separate branches or copies for each agent
Run dbt-core and gpt-engineer in non-overlapping phases
Check in generated files only after review
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can write files and offer to run generated code, so if it consumes dbt-core outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into code generation and execution. dbt-core's warehouse-facing outputs may be treated as facts, and gpt-engineer's execution authority makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer uses dbt-core outputs as authoritative inputs without verification
IF generated code is executed with the user's privileges
mitigations: Require human verification of dbt outputs before code generation
Disable automatic execution of generated code
Add schema and assertion checks between agents
Limit gpt-engineer to dry-run mode
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between dbt and code generation

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and gpt-engineer handles project files plus an OpenAI API key and external model calls. If warehouse data includes regulated records, moving it into gpt-engineer's external model path can create retention and residency mismatches, though the profiles do not prove a specific jurisdictional violation.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or files
IF the configured model backend retains prompts beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from prompts and files
Use a local or enterprise-approved model backend
Review retention settings for the configured API provider
Document data-handling boundaries for both agents
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
